instruction: Enable natural scrolling for the mouse in Ubuntu's settings.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling natural scrolling for mouse. Config sets natural-scroll to false initially, user must change it to true. Evaluator checks gsettings value is 'true'. No custom functions needed - uses existing get_vm_command_line getter and exact_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: executes 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.mouse natural-scroll' which retrieves the exact state required by the instruction
Metric comparison is correct: exact_match properly compares command output with expected value 'true\n'
Expected value is semantically correct: 'true\n' matches gsettings output format when natural scrolling is enabled
Complete coverage: evaluator fully verifies the single requirement (enable natural scrolling)
State accessibility: gsettings value can be queried at any time, no postconfig needed
Parameter handling is correct: exact_match function properly accesses rules['expected'] when type='rule'
Data flow is sound: config sets to false → user enables to true → evaluator checks for 'true\n'
